title: Firuz and His Virtuous Wife

full_text:
Following the King's public proclamation in the tribunal, Firuz and his wife returned to their garden mansion, their bond of affection and trust strengthened tenfold by the trial they had endured.

Firuz took his wife’s hands and asked with sincere humility: 'Forgive me, dear companion! Why did you bring the matter before the public tribunal rather than speaking to me in private?'

His wife smiled with profound wisdom and replied: 'O husband, a private whisper in the bedchamber might have left a lingering shadow of doubt in your heart, and slanderous tongues in the bazaar would have whispered that the King’s visit had compromised our honor.

By bringing our cause before the open assembly in the language of noble allegory, the King himself was compelled to stand as witness to my virtue, your honor was vindicated before all the ministers, and the sanctity of our household was established as a fortress of light.'

Firuz bowed before her extraordinary intellect and discernment. He realized that a wife endowed with moral courage and sharp wit is a greater treasure than all the jewels in the royal treasury.

The King appointed Firuz Grand Chancellor of the realm, and their home became a celebrated sanctuary where young couples came to learn that mutual respect, open truth, and moral dignity are the true foundations of enduring joy.
moral: A household founded on mutual trust and moral courage cannot be shaken by the greatest powers.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "Firuz and His Wife"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
